text:
ben-platform: heads-up — we saw a few SLO blips this morning when mobile clients hit a short fanout spike. The token-bucket per-key config let the requests through but our downstream batchers overloaded. wondering if we should add short-window hysteresis or tighten per-org burst caps. anyone seen this pattern?

alice-sre: yep, saw it in the dashboard. looks like a 15s spike that accounted for ~60% of errors. steady-state qps fine. :grimacing:

charlie-ops: quick recap of current setup: per-key token bucket with capacity=200, refill_rate=10/s. per-org global cap applied after bucket. we allow short bursts to avoid throttling UX.

ben-platform: problem is the burst interacts poorly with autoscaler warmup + batch size. short spikes cause more concurrent backpressure than token cost suggests. maybe add a very short leaky-bucket in front to smooth microbursts?

dina-ml: curious if we can do adaptive short-window rate-limit that counts only last 10s for burst decisions and still uses token bucket for long term? would need metric and cheap eval in our routing layer.

alice-sre: prototypes we ran before used a 5s EWMA on request rate and a separate short_window_capacity. if ewma > threshold then we limit burst tokens to X% for next Ys. that prevented spike storms.

ben-platform: can you paste the config snippet you used?

alice-sre: sure — simplified version:

```yaml
burst_policy:
  short_window_seconds: 5
  ewma_alpha: 0.4
  short_capacity_fraction: 0.25 # allow only 25% of normal bucket for 5s if spike detected
  cooldown_seconds: 10
```

charlie-ops: that helped, but we had edge cases where many keys in an org all used up their short capacity and then hit the org cap simultaneously. made the org cap the real bottleneck and kicked many requests.

ben-platform: hmm — so per-key short caps reduced per-key chaos but amplified org-level queuing. maybe we need a hierarchical token approach: reserve a tiny org-level reservoir for smoothing when many keys spike?

dina-ml: hierarchical tokens + backpressure hinting would be ideal. routing could attach a header like `X-Can-Queue: true/false` so callers can downgrade to async path instead of hot retrying.

charlie-ops: +1 on hint header. also consider jitter on refill to avoid synchronized refill waves across keys. we saw refills line up at second boundaries. add random offset in [0,1s].

ben-platform: good call. other ops: do we prefer token-bucket-with-short-leaky or pure leaky frontdoor? tradeoffs?

alice-sre: summary of tradeoffs:
- token-bucket with short-window cap = preserves UX for majority, easier to reason per-key, but complexity grows with hierarchical rules.
- leaky-frontdoor = smoother global ingress, simpler for autoscaler, but harsher on short legitimate bursts (risk UX regressions).

charlie-ops: i'd prefer hybrid: leaky frontdoor tuned to protect downstream + token buckets for per-key fairness. plus adaptive EWMA to detect anomalous traffic and lower short_capacity_fraction.

ben-platform: action items:
- charlie to prototype frontdoor leaky queue with jittered refill (PR by EOD Wed)
- alice to share EWMA-based short_window gating with example config and dashboard panels
- dina to draft routing header proposal for graceful async fallback (include SDK change request)
- I will run sim with multi-key burst scenarios to tune hierarchical reservoir sizes

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: eng-platform/burst-proto -> staging at 2026-03-18T11:20Z :rocket:

alice-sre: thanks — adding a panel to the burst-diagnostics dashboard to show short_window hit rate and org reservoir level.

dina-ml: i'll look at client SDK fallbacks after header proposal. could help reduce retries.

ben-platform: thanks all. we'll sync Fri to review results. :thumbsup:
